history.summary: The Arulmigu Eachanari Vinayagar Temple at Eachanari is one of the most visited Ganesha shrines in Tamil Nadu, famed for its large idol of Lord Vinayagar - about 6 feet tall and 3 feet wide, carved from a single stone. The temple's history dates to the 1500s: according to the temple legend, the idol was being carried on a cart from Madurai to be installed at the Patteeswarar Temple in Perur when the cart's axle broke down at Eachanari; the idol became embedded in the soil, which devotees read as a divine sign, and the temple was built around it on that spot. Built in the Dravidian style with a tall gopuram, the temple has been renovated several times - the first kumbabhishekam was held in 1977 and photographs of the ceremony are displayed in the temple. It is a hugely popular shrine for prayers to remove obstacles and bring success, and a noted stop for devotees seeking blessings for new vehicles (per devotee reviews - verify). The temple is administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department.

name: Eachanari Vinayagar Temple
town: Eachanari (CSV town 'Coimbatore' - the temple is at Eachanari on the Pollachi highway, ~12 km from Coimbatore city)
town_description: Eachanari is a village-turned-suburban locality on the Coimbatore-Pollachi highway (NH 209), about 12 km south of Coimbatore city centre, adjoining the SIDCO Industrial Estate (Pin 641021). The Vinayagar temple stands right on the highway - currently under the flyover - which makes it a natural halt for travellers but means parking is tight.

travel.airport: Coimbatore International Airport (approx. 15 km; taxis and app cabs available). (verify)
travel.railway: Coimbatore Junction (approx. 9 km, per the temple's official site).
travel.road: On the Coimbatore-Pollachi highway (NH 209) at Eachanari, ~12 km from Coimbatore city centre; reachable by city buses, taxis and autos - public transport is often easier than driving because of the tight roadside parking.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Vinayaka Chaturthi (August-September) is the biggest annual festival, drawing thousands; Fridays and Sankatahara Chaturthi are especially busy.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT - one local guide citing the temple's official HR&CE site (checked September 2026) says the temple is open 5:00 AM-10:00 PM daily with no midday break; other listings report 5:30 AM-1:00 PM and 3:00/4:00 PM-10:00 PM. (verify) Entry is free; modest dress advised.
